title: Improved estimate of local Markovianity for quantum Gibbs states
abstract: We establish improved locally Markovian properties of quantum Gibbs states at every fixed positive temperature. For finite-range interactions of bounded interaction degree, the conditional mutual information (CMI) decays exponentially with separation, with a prefactor exponential in the boundary size. This improves the exponential volume dependence of the local Markov bounds established by Chen and Rouzé \cite{Chen2025}. For exponentially and stretched-exponentially decaying interactions, we obtain stretched-exponential CMI decay with a boundary-dependent prefactor. For power-law interactions, we prove inverse-logarithmic or algebraic decay with polynomial region-size dependence. Our proof is static, in contrast to the dynamical approach of Chen and Rouzé. We compare the Gibbs state with a product state obtained by removing boundary interactions, reducing the CMI bound to a relative-entropy loss that we control using locality estimates.
summary: This work provides rigorous, improved estimates for how local quantum correlations decay in quantum Gibbs states. By analyzing the Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) for different interaction types, the authors show that the decay rate depends on the boundary size rather than the volume, which is a significant theoretical advance for characterizing quantum locality.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish improved, quantitative estimates for the local Markovian properties of quantum Gibbs states.
main_result: It derives specific decay rates for the Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) based on the decay type of the interactions (finite-range, stretched-exponential, or power-law).
method: The analysis uses a static approach, bounding the CMI by relating it to a relative-entropy loss, which is then controlled using variational methods and resolvent identities.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum lattice model described by a Hamiltonian $H_{\Lambda}$, and the state is the quantum Gibbs state $ho_{\Lambda,  eta} = e^{- eta H_{\Lambda}} / 	ext{Tr} e^{- eta H_{\Lambda}}$.
key_observables: Conditional Mutual Information (CMI), Relative Entropy Loss ($\delta_R(ho, \sigma)$), and the cut interaction strength ($g_{A|Ac}$).
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), separation distance ($r$), and the decay exponents ($\zeta, 	heta$) characterizing the interaction decay.
main_assumptions: The results hold for fixed positive temperature ($ eta > 0$) and rely on bounding the interaction strength across a spatial cut.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares its derived bounds (for finite-range, quasi-local, and power-law interactions) against prior work, utilizing variational calculus and resolvent identities to control the relative entropy loss.
why_interesting: The improved, boundary-dependent bounds on CMI are crucial for understanding quantum correlations and locality in thermal quantum many-body systems, which is central to modern condensed matter theory.
